To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ratio of the range to the standard deviation of a sample from a normal population is approximately normally distributed.

(a) the ratio of two sample ranges from independent normal populations is approximately normally distributed, with the mean of the distribution being the square root of the ratio of the population standard deviations and the variance of the distribution being equal to the ratio of the variances, (b) the distribution is symmetric and (c) it is possible to construct a confidence interval for the population ratio of standard deviations.
the sampling distribution of the ratio is skewed to the left for all sample sizes, and is skewed to the right for all sample sizes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the joint sampling distributions and the sampling distributions of the ratio of ranges from two independent samples.
the sampling distribution of the ratio, r, of two ranges from independent samples, where the two populations have the same variance, and where the ratio of sample sizes, n2/n, is fixed at 2, 3, or 4.
the sampling distribution of the ratio, r, of two ranges from independent random samples drawn from the same normal population.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ratio of two range values from independent samples is distributed approximately as the ratio of two independent random variables.

the sampling distribution of the ratio, r, of two ranges is the same as that of the ratio of their means, provided that the ratio is not greater than 1 and that the two ranges are drawn independently.
the sampling distribution of the ratio r = (xn - xl)/(xn - x2) is a function of the sample size n and the ratio r.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the sampling distribution of the ratio r of two ranges from independent samples may be obtained from the joint sampling distribution by integration over all values of w, except the values of w which make r = 0.
we have shown the sampling distributions of the ratio of ranges, the ratio of ranges to the range, and the ratio of ranges squared to the square of the range.
the ratio of two independent ranges is approximately distributed as a ratio of two independent chi-square variables, with the same degrees of freedom as the ranges.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in general, the distribution of a ratio of ranges is not a function of the ratio of variances.
we have developed a method that can be used to estimate the sampling distribution of the ratio between two sample means from independent samples.
we should not be too quick to dismiss the use of the range as a measure of spread.
